chunks: Abān ibn Taghlib narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

"The best of my Ummah are those who, when they travel, break their fast and shorten [the salat], and when they do good, they rejoice, and when they do wrong, they seek forgiveness. And the worst of my Ummah are those who were born in luxury and nourished in it: they eat fine food, wear soft clothes, and when they speak, they do not speak truthfully."

key_terms.أَفْطَرُوا: they broke the fast during travel
key_terms.اسْتَبْشَرُوا: they rejoiced and were gladdened by their good deeds
key_terms.اسْتَغْفَرُوا: they sought Allah's forgiveness after wrongdoing
key_terms.قَصَّرُوا: they shortened the salat while traveling

ai.seo_question: Who are described as the best and worst of the Ummah in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith praises believers who accept the divine concession during travel by breaking the fast and shortening the salat, and who respond to good deeds with joy and to sins with seeking forgiveness. It also condemns those absorbed in luxury whose outward comfort is joined with moral corruption, especially dishonesty in speech.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1978 - Aban ibn Taghlib narrated from Abu Ja'far (as), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"The best among my nation are those who break their fast and shorten their prayers when traveling, rejoice when they do good, and seek forgiveness when they commit wrongs. The worst among my nation are those who are born into luxury, nurtured in it, eat the finest food, wear the softest clothes, and do not speak truthfully when they speak."
